# 160-puzzle difficulty scoring run

Generated 20 classic Sudoku puzzles at each requested tier using the updated engine in this worktree. The original generation run used scoring version 14. The current engine re-solved all 160 puzzles under classic scoring version 15 and structured variant version 24; every puzzle still solves at its requested tier and every recorded action agrees with a complete solution. Scores use evidence-sensitive costs: 3D Medusa scales with colored candidate nodes (10-node reference), direct Unique Rectangle deductions scale with the total candidate count across their four corners (nine-candidate reference), and UR1 has a lower subtype reference cost. Difficulty-tier matching still follows the hardest technique tier and selected solver profile; point totals do not choose the tier.

The per-puzzle table below preserves the original generated puzzle set and its top-five trace details. Its listed point totals are the version 14 generation scores. The current version 15 score ranges and hardest-technique distribution are summarized next; only four puzzles contain UR1, and the trace order and technique sequence are unchanged.

## Current score ranges and hardest techniques

Each row summarizes the 20 puzzles in that requested tier. Point ranges are the minimum and maximum of the version 15 evidence-adjusted totals; the median is included to show the center. “Hardest techniques” lists which technique was highest in each trace, with puzzle counts. The per-puzzle tables below list the five latest distinct techniques in solver order, so they show the actual upper end of each recorded path as well.

| Requested tier | Point range (median) | Hardest technique used across the 20 puzzles |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Medium | 724–1,092 (821) | Naked Pair 7; Claiming 5; Naked Triple 4; Locked Triple 2; Hidden Pair 1; Pointing 1 |
| Tricky | 784–1,308 (1,010) | Skyscraper 10; Two-String Kite 5; X-Wing 5 |
| Hard | 800–1,536 (1,127) | W-Wing 11; XY-Wing 4; BUG+1 2; XYZ-Wing 2; Unique Rectangle 1 1 |
| Very Hard | 1,396–5,907 (2,241) | 3D Medusa 10; XY-Chain 8; Finned Swordfish 1; X-Chain 1 |
| Expert | 1,780–8,417 (3,280) | AIC 20 |
| Master | 3,841–26,167 (8,271) | Grouped AIC 7; ALS-XY-Wing 5; ALS-XZ 5; ALS-Chain 2; Unique Rectangle AIC 1 |
| Extreme | 1,482–24,517 (10,018) | Forcing Chain 15; Forcing Net 4; Multi-Sector Locked Sets 1 |
| Impossible | 78,432–162,134 (107,469) | Nested Forcing Net 10; Quadruple Pattern Overlay 6; Quintuple Pattern Overlay 4 |

These ranges overlap between neighboring tiers. That is expected: the label represents the hardest technique tier, while point totals estimate accumulated evidence-weighted work. For example, a short Impossible path can have fewer points than a long Extreme path without changing either path's hardest-technique tier.

“Hardest techniques used” lists the five latest distinct technique IDs present in the selected logical solve trace, ordered by the solver profile. It describes this recorded solve path; it does not establish that every alternative valid solve path must use those techniques.

The run contained 67 direct Unique Rectangle deductions. Candidate totals across the four corners ranged from 9 to 17 (median 11), producing evidence-adjusted costs from 100 to 188 points. Technique counts: hidden-rectangle 48, unique-rectangle-1 4, unique-rectangle-2 1, unique-rectangle-3 1, unique-rectangle-4 7, unique-rectangle-6 6.
